newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso bounces back, banks sell dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso bounces back, banks sell dlrs.

text.p: * Expected drop in Central Bank's rate not materializing
The Philippine peso rose on Thursday after the Central Bank's resolve not to drop its interest rates pushed banks into selling their dollars, traders said on Thursday.
The peso closed at 26.265 to the dollar from 26.269, with the day's average at 26.265 from 26.268.
"Speculators did not have any choice but to unload dollars they've been hoarding over a week," said a dealer.
Banks had expected the Central Bank to reduce its overnight rates after inflation dropped to 4.4 percent in September from 7.9 in August. That would have made the dollar more attractive to hold.
"It's costly for banks to hold on to their long dollar positions," said another dealer.
Moreover, dealers said the Central Bank was firm in selling dollars at 26.27 the past sessions.
One dealer estimated the Central Bank was a dominant buyer in the market this Thursday with a volume of $70 million.
Turnover rose to $180 million from $127.10 million.
